title: Processor kept a scam merchant with an 8.5% chargeback rate (FTC v. Nuvei)

source.ref: FTC press release and complaint, Nuvei settlement ($4.85M), September 2026

narrative: The FTC alleges a processor kept an offshore tech-support merchant (Reimage) on for years. An internal risk report showed an annual chargeback rate above 8.5% in 2021 (1,108 chargebacks on 12,934 sales). The merchant shifted volume to other processors so its account would not stay on a card-network monitoring list.
diagnosis: Merchant-level fraud with chargebacks managed down by splitting volume, not by fixing the cause

outcome.summary: Public record: the FTC sued; the processor agreed to pay $4.85M and adopt merchant screening and monitoring. No merchant-level after numbers.

title: 29-40% of a merchant's charges disputed as fraud (FTC v. BlueSnap)

source.ref: FTC press release, BlueSnap settlement ($10M), May 2024

narrative: The FTC alleges a processor kept processing for a debt-relief merchant even though Visa reports showed 29% to 40% of its charges disputed as fraudulent, another processor had advised closing the accounts, and a card network asked for them to be shut. Processing continued for more than a year.
diagnosis: Fraudulent merchant: disputes are a symptom of deception, not of operations

outcome.summary: Public record: $10M settlement and a ban on processing for certain high-risk categories. The lower bound 29% is used as the dispute rate; the fraud share is inferred from 'disputed as fraudulent'.

title: Multiple accounts and sham chargeback-reduction plans (FTC v. CMS)

source.ref: FTC press release, Complete Merchant Solutions settlement ($1.5M), December 2020

narrative: The FTC alleges a processor ignored red flags: high consumer chargeback rates, merchants using multiple merchant accounts to artificially lower chargeback rates and avoid detection by banks and card networks, and sham chargeback-reduction plans.
diagnosis: Chargeback rates hidden rather than reduced

outcome.summary: Public record: $1.5M settlement. Lesson for Precedent: splitting volume across accounts to lower a reported rate is a red flag, never a remedy.

title: Merchant matched evidence to reason codes; contested win rate about 28% to 60%

source.ref: Shopify Community thread by a merchant, June 2026, with replies
source.licence: Third-party forum post; summarised and cited, not reproduced

narrative: A merchant contested about 60% of chargebacks and won about 28% of those, submitting only order confirmations. After learning each reason code's evidence requirements (for example device and purchase-history data for fraud codes), the merchant reported a win rate of about 60% over the next three months.
diagnosis: Wrong evidence for the reason code

outcome.summary: Self-reported: contested win rate about 28% to about 60% in three months. Replies note a confound: win rate covers only contested disputes, so part of the gain may be case selection. Not a dispute-rate change.
